candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — antepartum/intrapartum/postpartum and newborn care, caregiver education, and interventions that promote normal newborn adaptation and development
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — newborn skin-to-skin care
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize skin-to-skin care as a health-promoting practice that supports newborn thermoregulation and breastfeeding while still requiring safe monitoring and sleep practices.

options.A: Support of newborn temperature stability and early breastfeeding opportunities
options.B: Elimination of the need for routine newborn monitoring while skin-to-skin
options.C: Prevention of all neonatal hypoglycemia regardless of maternal or infant risk factors
options.D: Safe substitution for a bassinet when the parent becomes sleepy or wants to sleep

candidate.rationale: AAP guidance supports immediate skin-to-skin care for stable mother/newborn dyads and describes benefits including improved temperature stability and support for breastfeeding, with other physiologic benefits reported. Skin-to-skin does not eliminate the need for appropriate observation, does not guarantee prevention of hypoglycemia, and is not a safe sleep arrangement when the caregiver is asleep or unable to respond. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For stable dyads, skin-to-skin care supports thermoregulation and breastfeeding opportunities but does not replace monitoring or safe-sleep precautions.
candidate.source_document_title: Safe Sleep and Skin-to-Skin Care in the Neonatal Period for Healthy Term Newborns; Policy Statement: Breastfeeding and the Use of Human Milk
candidate.source_locator: Safe Sleep and Skin-to-Skin Care > Evidence for SSC and Rooming-In: immediate SSC stabilizes newborn body temperature and supports physiologic stability; Procedure/monitoring section: dyad monitored and infant moved to bassinet or awake support person when mother wants to sleep. Breastfeeding policy: immediate skin-to-skin care is among maternity practices associated with improved breastfeeding initiation
candidate.source_version_date: AAP clinical report/policy statements remain current; pages accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: A stable term newborn is placed skin-to-skin with an awake, medically stable parent shortly after birth. Which outcome is a recognized benefit of this practice?
